m:elbphi: The Plaza is open every day from 10am to midnight (last entry 11:30pm). The ticket to go up costs €5 per person (€3 reduced for ages 3 to 17 and students), bought online or at the Ticket Pavilion in front of the building; booking online guarantees entry at your chosen time without queuing (on the Elbphilharmonie website). Concert ticket holders can go up to the Plaza up to two hours before. Check winter hours and closures for events on elbphilharmonie.de.
m:speicher: Free to walk around at any time of day. Boats on the Speicherstadt canals depend on the tide and are paid (check prices and times on the operator's website). In the evening the buildings are lit up and the district is very atmospheric. Some warehouses house small museums (customs, coffee, spices) with their own hours.
m:wunder: Open every day of the year, at least from 9:30am to 6pm; at weekends, during school holidays and on some evenings hours are longer (calendar on the website). Tickets have an entry time chosen online: without booking you risk a long wait. The base adult price starts at about €22 (from guides and a partial official page: confirm on miniatur-wunderland.com). At weekends and in holidays it costs more and sells out.
m:rathaus: The square and the boulevard are free to see. Inside the Rathaus you can only go on a paid guided tour (usually in German and English, a few times a day; check times and prices on the city website). From late November the square usually hosts the Christmas market (2026 dates to be confirmed).
m:michel: In winter the tower is open every day from 10am to 5:30pm (from a tourist listing, to be confirmed). Tower climb €5, crypt with exhibition and film €4, combined ticket €7; slightly cheaper with the Hamburg Card. The lift goes halfway up the tower, the rest is a short flight of stairs. The nave can be visited for a small donation, outside services.
m:nikolai: Entry with the climb starts at €11.90 (tourist listing, to be confirmed). Winter hours not checked: look on mahnmal-st-nikolai.de before going. The outdoor ruins are free to see.
m:landung: The harbour boat tour takes about an hour: prices range from €17 to €26 depending on the company; from November to Easter departures are every hour or half hour, roughly from 10–11am to 3–5pm (list from the Hamburg tourism website, not guaranteed: to be confirmed). To save money, HVV ferry line 62 crosses the harbour with a normal public transport ticket. The Old Elbe Tunnel is free on foot; check the city website for any work on the lift. On Sunday mornings, nearby, there's the Fischmarkt, the fish market, very early (winter hours to be confirmed: usually 7 to 9:30am).
m:reeper: By day you can walk around without problems; in the evening and at weekends the area gets very crowded, with noisy bars: always keep bags and phones close. You can see it all for free from the pavement. Avoid side streets late at night.
m:kontor: Free to see from the street at any time of day; the office interiors are not open. The Chilehaus has a courtyard with a few shops open during the day.
m:kunsthalle: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, Thursday until 9pm; closed on Mondays (hours from an online listing, confirm on hamburger-kunsthalle.de). The ticket costs about €14 (price not checked: to be confirmed); under-18s go free.
m:planten: Entry to the park is free and it's open all year from 7am until late (winter hours to be confirmed). The tropical greenhouses have a separate ticket, while the evening water shows are only in the warm season: in winter there usually aren't any.
vd:paris: A French-style brasserie in a former late-19th-century dairy shop, all tiles and mirrors, a short walk from the Rathaus. Good for a big breakfast or a lunch of simple dishes.
vp:paris: Breakfast costs about €10–16 and a dish of the day €14–22 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:ratswein: The Rathaus cellar, with brick vaults dating from 1897: Hamburg cooking with fish, Labskaus and Pannfisch, and a good wine list. A place for a proper meal, cheaper than most restaurants on the lakefront.
vp:ratswein: A main course is around €16–26 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:wischer: A fish sandwich counter on Spitalerstraße, the pedestrian street between the station and the centre: Fischbrötchen with herring, salmon and prawns, eaten standing up, for a quick and typical Hamburg lunch.
vp:wischer: A fish sandwich costs about €4–8 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:bruecke10: The most famous fish kiosk at the Landungsbrücken: Fischbrötchen with herring, Backfisch (fried fish) or salmon, with a view of the harbour. It's Hamburg's signature lunch, eaten standing on the pier.
vp:bruecke10: A fish sandwich costs about €5–9 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:ocr: A traditional tavern near the Michel, open since 1795, popular with sailors and harbour traders: dark wood, paintings of ships and a plate of Labskaus (mashed potato, salt beef and beetroot) or Pannfisch.
vp:ocr: A main course costs about €18–30 (menu not seen): pricier than the beer halls. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:groeninger: A brewpub in a brick cellar a few steps from the Michel and the Nikolaikirche: home-brewed beer and northern German dishes, with generous portions and mid-range prices.
vp:groeninger: A dish with a beer is around €18–26 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:albrecht: A brewery-restaurant in the centre, near the Rathaus, with beer brewed on site and a menu of Hamburg and northern German dishes: Schnitzel, Labskaus and sausages.
vp:albrecht: A main course costs about €15–24 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:gnosa: One of the first cafés in St. Georg, open since 1978, on Lange Reihe, the street of shops and bars close to the central station: breakfasts, homemade cakes and light dishes.
vp:gnosa: Breakfast is around €9–14 and a slice of cake €5–6 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:fleet: A small brick building on a Speicherstadt canal, with tables on the water: coffee, cakes, Fischbrötchen and a few simple dishes, ideal for a break between the Speicherstadt and HafenCity.
vp:fleet: A coffee with a pastry is around €7–10 and a fish sandwich €6–10 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:schanzen: An alternative café-restaurant in the Sternschanze district, run by a local cooperative: big breakfasts, dishes with organic ingredients and many vegetarian options. Low prices in a lively neighbourhood.
vp:schanzen: Breakfast costs about €8–12 and a dish of the day €11–16 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:maritimo: Ten floors of ship models, uniforms and paintings in an old Speicherstadt warehouse.
cd:ballin: The barracks from which five million Europeans left for America.
cx:ballin: It's in Veddel, about 5 km from the centre.
cd:dialogo: An hour in total darkness with a blind guide.
cd:mkg: Decorative arts, design and fashion in a building next to the station.
cd:rickmer: An 1896 three-master moored by the harbour.
cd:speichermuseo: How people worked in the Speicherstadt's coffee and spice warehouses.
cd:uboot: A Soviet Cold War submarine you can go inside.
cd:hagenbeck: A zoo with bar-free enclosures and an Asian temple.
cd:alster: An hour on the inner lake among villas, gardens and canals.
